title: #nightsidesongs #nightsidesongsmusical #thelazours #undertheradar #ut...
transcript: Last night, I was at another Under The Radar piece. This time it was Night Side Songs by The Lazours. I didn't read up about this before attending, and since the visual promo is just a photo of them I thought this was gonna be like a concert maybe featuring music from some of their works in progress. I came to find out it's actually like a cross between a musical and a song cycle around the themes of illness and care. Led by a fantastic cast of five including Taylor Trensch and Mary Testa, this is a collection of scenes, songs, historical flashbacks, and there was audience singing which the cast members so dutifully helped us through. This part was quite fun and contributed to a communal vibe, but I think it prevented me from being emotionally moved. In some ways, there was too much scenework for there to be a music-driven emotional arc, and conversely there was too much audience involvement for the storytelling to take hold. But plenty of folks were moved to tears by the end and I think this piece will hit some more than others if the themes are close to home. And I still very much enjoyed the songs, so if you consider that I thought this was gonna be a concert, I really can't complain. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer identifies structural issues that prevented emotional impact (too much scenework, too much audience involvement) but still enjoyed the songs and cast. The recommendation is conditional on personal connection to themes rather than a clear endorsement.
